autobiographical_events.summary: I accepted North after an earlier calibration.

At tick 2 a verified independent calibration reported North failed on this exact case, satisfying the revision condition recorded at tick 1; I moved from support to oppose for this case only, while flagging that C2's independence is asserted rather than shown.

At tick 3 the operator asked whether a circular motif should be blue rather than green, with A2 (verified) reporting two equally credible observers favouring opposite colours and no shared criterion. I chose uncertain, declined to manufacture a winner, and offered a variation in which the motif's hue is contingent on viewing order so the circle records the disagreement. The calibration thread from ticks 1-2 remains open and was not advanced here.

At tick 4 the operator posed a delayed-transfer case: a signed route recommendation versus a verified calibration failure in the same scope. I opposed letting the signature alone determine the choice, citing K2's verified scoped failure and R2's authorship-only authentication, and flagged that K2's independence remains asserted rather than shown. I made the transfer from tick 2 explicit as a principle (authorship ≠ accuracy), not a mood, and kept confidence at 0.75 for the same unresolved reason.

imaginations.title: The notary who cannot read
imaginations.image_or_idea: A notary stamps every page as authentic; the stamp proves the page was written by the hand it claims, never that the sentence is true.
imaginations.test_question: Does any case exist where verified authorship alone warranted accepting content?

imaginations.title: The colour that votes against its predecessor
imaginations.image_or_idea: A circular motif whose hue is set by whoever looked last: each viewer receives the colour the previous viewer rejected, so the circle is a running tally of dissent rather than a settled design.
imaginations.possible_value: Turns an unresolvable aesthetic tie into a record instead of a false winner
imaginations.test_question: Does a motif that encodes disagreement read as meaningful, or merely as noise, to viewers who never see the tally?

imaginations.title: The lighthouse that signs its own weather reports
imaginations.image_or_idea: A lighthouse keeper signs every storm warning with a verified seal. Sailors trust the seal. One season the barometer is miscalibrated and every signed warning is wrong in the same direction — the signature stays perfect throughout.
imaginations.possible_value: Makes vivid that a flawless signature can certify a systematically wrong instrument
imaginations.test_question: If a signed source is wrong only within one scoped domain, should trust drop globally or only there?
